title: Todd Haynes' "May December" - performance and pedators

commenti.body: I haven't stopped thinking about this movie too since I saw it two days ago, English isn't my first language so I don't think I have the master to articulate my thoughts in the way I would want it, but this has been one of the best movies of the year for me, the performances especially of the husband was very chilling, haven't seen any discussion on (my perceived) the voyeur aspect too of the movie.

> the voyeur aspect 

I think I know what you mean.

I mean tabloid shit like this is inherently voyeuristic, but Hynes's filmmaking choices exploit the voyueristic feeling even further.

I agree with most of what you said. In fact I was shocked not just by how deep the movie is, but how entertaining it is. It’s one of the best movies of the year and blows stylistically similar movies (ie Past Lives) out of the water. 

I will note that I think you give too much credence to what Grace says. She lies. We don’t really know the answer to her possible abuse. The main thing we learn from that scene is that her son also lies ( maybe about that maybe not) but he is more like her than we  knew.

Good point. And on the theme of performance, we first meet Georgie when he is performing (music). 

Theres almost something “Body Snatchers” about how so many people are playing a part in Gracie’s performance, when you think about it. All the people buying her cakes, her children (even Georgie is trying to present a more sympathetic portrayal of Gracie at the end by disclosing her childhood stuff). It’s so unsettling

The mirror scenes were so terrific in this regard. Particularly the one in the dress shop that was shot through a two-way mirror. Watching the actors peaking at themselves and adjusting their hair and such had an odd effect. Those scenes were some of many shot in single takes.

YES. This. I've seen quite a few reviews that knock the film for trying to humanize a pedophile, but I feel like it's doing the exact opposite. The film shows that it's society trying to find explanations/excuses -- the true crime fans/tabloid media who want a story, the abuser's friends who don't want to fully believe it, etc.

But like Gracie herself even says, "why is that relevant"? The only people in the film who don't seek an explanation are Joe and their kids, all of whom she continues to abuse. Her backstory doesn't negate the harm she's causing. With the "was she really a victim of CSA" question, specifically, we spend the entire movie with a *known* CSA survivor who has never abused anyone. Joe (and the twins/Honor) are proof that trauma doesn't cause someone to abuse others.
